finalists.label: Pyknodysostosis
finalists.why: It has the most specific and detailed evidence for its diagnosis, including frontal bossing, prominent forehead, large open anterior fontanel, micrognathia, high nasal bridge, broad philtrum, short terminal phalanges with bulbous fingertips, and broad, spoon-shaped nails, as well as diffuse osteosclerosis, biconvex vertebrae, a wide open anterior fontanel with Wormian bones, and acro-osteolysis of the distal phalanges.

finalists.label: Achondroplasia
finalists.why: It is a strong candidate due to its proportionate short stature, height, weight, and upper-to-lower body segment ratio, but it lacks specific evidence for diffuse osteosclerosis and other skeletal findings.

finalists.label: Cleidocranial dysplasia
finalists.why: It shares some features with Pyknodysostosis, such as frontal bossing and large open anterior fontanel, but lacks specific evidence for diffuse osteosclerosis and other distinctive skeletal findings.

frontier_selector.why: The champion, Pyknodysostosis, is chosen due to its comprehensive and specific evidence, including both clinical and radiological findings, which are not fully explained by the other candidates.
